topic: Classifying Objects and Materials as Solid, Liquid, Gas
key_concepts: Matter is anything that has weight and takes up space.
Matter exists in three states: solid, liquid, and gas.
Solids have observable characteristics: color, size, shape, and texture.
Solids can be classified by color, size, shape, and texture.
Solid shapes include round, square, rectangle, triangle, and oblong.
Solid textures include rough, smooth, hard, and soft.
Solid size can be measured using a ruler or meter stick.
Liquids take the shape of their container and can flow.
Liquids occupy space and have weight.
Gases cannot always be seen but can be felt and are around us.
Gases have weight, occupy space, and have no definite shape or size.
Air is an example of gas; water is an example of liquid.
